passage.label: No soul reached collar bones; said who cure; dying certain time separation; leg wound about leg; Lord Day procession; disbeliever not believed nor prayed; denied turned away; went people swaggering pride; Woe you woe; Then woe you woe

mainSubject.label: When the soul reaches the collar bones and it is asked who will cure him, the dying one becomes certain it is the time of separation with leg wound about leg; to the Lord that Day is the procession; the disbeliever neither believed nor prayed but denied and turned away, going to his people swaggering in pride; repeated woe pronounced upon him

subordinateSubjects.label: When the soul has reached the collar bones
And it is asked who will cure him
The dying one is certain it is the time of separation
And the leg is wound about the leg
To your Lord that Day will be the procession
The disbeliever had not believed nor had he prayed
But instead he denied and turned away
And went to his people swaggering in pride
Then woe to you, and woe

humanConditionsAndSpiritualStates.label: Soul reaching collar bones with no cure available and certainty of separation
Leg wound about leg marking the final moment before procession to the Lord
Disbelief combined with prayer neglect, denial, turning away and swaggering pride

socialEconomicCivilisational.label: Swaggering return to people after denial identified as grounds for repeated woe

relationships.label: Procession to the Lord on that Day as the universal destination

notes: Wave 11 genuine re-extraction. Boundaries follow the text: P1 closes with the self-witness and excuses statement (15) before the Quran-recitation instruction opens (16); P2 ends with the contorted-faces-backbreaking-expectation scene (25) before the deathbed sequence begins (26); P3 runs through collar-bones, separation certainty, leg-wound, procession and the swaggering-denier woe (26-35); P4 covers the neglected-question, embryological stages and the closing resurrection-ability argument (36-40).
